title: Forth
transcript:
[The right rear portion of a car is shown. On the bumper is a sticker that says:]
I FORTH ❤️
explanation:
is a  . Like most stack-oriented programming languages, Forth's grammar incorporates . For example, instead of an expression that adds two numbers via , such as 8 + 5, Forth would denote it as 8 5 +, indicating that the value "8" is pushed onto the stack, then a value of "5", then the operation "+" will take these latest two items from the stack and push their sum (the value 13) back onto it. Reverse Polish notation is not just limited to mathematical expressions in the language; control flow and function calls also analogously follow this notation.

This is similar to , where a statement in English using , as in "Sam ate apples", can be represented as "Sam apples ate".

The comic features a car with a  that mentions Forth, but in a way where the message reflects its grammar as a self-referential joke. The bumper sticker is a take on a common type with the format "I ❤️ [object]", where the object is what the driver publicly expresses personal attachment to. The heart symbol is an abbreviation of the word "love". A real-life example is the abbreviated form of the slogan "", expressed as "I ❤️ NY". In this case, instead of the expected "I ❤️ FORTH", the sticker reads "I FORTH ❤️" to reference Forth's stack-based logic and grammar. It could be interpreting "❤️" as a "word" that takes two arguments, SUBJECT OBJECT, and returns the statement "SUBJECT love(s) OBJECT".

While probably coincidental, as xkcd primarily uses uppercase, the capitalization of the word "FORTH" also parallels the convention of how the name was stylized in its early years until the late 1970s. This sometimes causes it to be mistakenly assumed to be an acronym, akin to other programming languages from its time like  and .

The title text is a similar joke, but this time expressing fondness towards reverse Polish notation. In Forth, not all Forth operators take two arguments. For example, NEGATE returns the negative of the previous argument, such that 1 NEGATE results in -1. This logic could apply to adjectives, where adjectives take one argument as a noun. This is similar to how the English word order "adjective–noun phrase" becomes the  "noun phrase–adjective". Thus, the two adjectives POLISH and REVERSE after the word NOTATION, result in "I NOTATION POLISH REVERSE ❤️", which is interpreted as "I love Reverse Polish Notation".

1033: Formal Logic also features a bumper sticker on a car, which involves personal expression. Reverse Polish notation is also the subject of 645: RPS.
